overview:
This private three-day journey crosses southern Morocco from west to east and then north: from Ouarzazate, the gateway to the desert, along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs to the gorges of the Dades and Todra, into the Erg Chebbi dunes for a night in a Sahara camp, and over the Middle Atlas to the imperial city of Fes. It is a one-way route, so you see something new every hour and finish in Fes, ready to continue your trip to the north, rather than driving back the way you came.

The first day is gentle: the palm grove and 17th-century kasbah of Skoura, the Valley of Roses at Kelaat M'Gouna and an evening in the Dades valley among red rock formations. On the second day you walk through the Todra gorge, where the walls rise about 300 m, cross the oases of the Tafilalet and ride a camel into the dunes at sunset to sleep in a desert camp under the stars. On the third day you watch the sun rise over the Sahara, then drive north through the palm-filled Ziz valley, the high plateaus of Midelt and the cedar forest of the Middle Atlas, where Barbary macaques live wild, to reach Fes in the late afternoon.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
• Start: Ouarzazate (hotel, airport or bus station) – Finish: your riad or hotel in Fes
• Type: private tour with your own driver
• Distance: about 850 km in total; Day 3 is the longest (about 470 km, a full day with stops)
• Nights: Dades valley (hotel), Erg Chebbi (desert camp)
• Meals: dinner and breakfast both nights
• Activity level: easy; short walks and a camel ride of about 1.5 hours each way

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Skoura palm grove and the Kasbah Amridil.
• Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses.
• The Dades valley with its 'monkey fingers' rocks and the hairpin road of Tisdrine.
• The Todra gorge and the long palm grove of Tinghir.
• The Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and sunrise, and a night in a desert camp.
• The Ziz valley, Midelt, the cedar forest near Azrou and Ifrane.

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
Ouarzazate is already halfway to the desert, so starting here saves the long drive over the Atlas from Marrakech and gives you a relaxed first day. Ending in Fes rather than returning west means no backtracking and makes it easy to continue to Chefchaouen, Tangier or a flight home. The two nights are well placed: the Dades for the canyons and the Sahara camp for the dunes.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Travellers already in Ouarzazate, for example after visiting Ait Ben Haddou or the film studios; couples and families who want the desert without a loop back; and anyone heading north to Fes and the Mediterranean coast.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To return to Ouarzazate, choose the [4-day Ouarzazate Sahara loop](/en-US/morocco/ouarzazate/tours/4-day-ouarzazate-to-merzouga-desert-tour-a-sahara-loop-via-dades-and-zagora/7c218caf46b760fcc098931b). With only two days, the [2-day tour from Ouarzazate to Merzouga](/en-US/morocco/ouarzazate/tours/2-day-tour-from-ouarzazate-to-merzouga-skoura-dades-todra-gorges/5dadd9a9ef01706f9ee87e75) reaches the dunes faster.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack layers: days are warm in the south, but desert nights are cold from November to March and the Middle Atlas can see snow in winter. Bring a small overnight bag for the camp, sunglasses, sunscreen and a scarf against the wind. Lunches, drinks and entrance fees (Kasbah Amridil, a few dirhams) are not included.
descriptions:
What to expect: an easy first day east along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs – the palm grove of Skoura, the Valley of Roses and an evening in the Dades valley.

Your driver picks you up in Ouarzazate at 09:00, from your hotel, the airport or the bus station. The road follows the valley east between the High Atlas and the Jebel Saghro, past earthen villages and kasbahs. After about 40 km you reach Skoura, one of the largest palm groves of the south, where you walk under the date palms to the Kasbah Amridil, a 17th-century fortified family house. Its tower rooms, olive press, granary and old kitchen tools show how a great southern household lived. Continue to Kelaat M'Gouna, in the Valley of Roses, where small Damask roses are picked in spring and distilled into rose water; the cooperatives sell it all year and the town celebrates its rose festival in May. In the afternoon you turn north at Boumalne into the Dades valley, where the river runs between red and ochre rocks. Your driver stops at the rounded formations called the 'monkey fingers' and, if the light is good, drives up to the hairpin bends of Tisdrine for the view, before you settle into your hotel above the river for dinner.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up in Ouarzazate.
10:00 – Skoura palm grove and Kasbah Amridil (about 1 hour).
12:00 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses; lunch (not included).
15:00 – Dades valley, the 'monkey fingers' and the Tisdrine viewpoint.
17:30 – Hotel in the Dades; dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The rose harvest is in late April and May; out of season you still find rose water and creams in the cooperatives.
• If you have not yet seen Ait Ben Haddou or the Atlas film studios, we can add one of them before leaving Ouarzazate.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, entrance fees, tips.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: dinner.

What to expect: a walk through the Todra gorge, the oases of the Tafilalet, and a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi at sunset for a night in a desert camp.

After breakfast you leave the Dades for Tinghir, a town of earthen ksour along one of the longest palm groves in the region. The road then enters the Todra gorge, where the limestone walls rise about 300 m and close to around ten metres apart at the narrowest point. You walk along the clear stream through the narrows, often with climbers on the rock above. The road east crosses stony plains past the khettaras, lines of wells that mark underground water channels dug centuries ago to irrigate the oases, and reaches Erfoud, known for its dates and the fossil workshops where marble full of ammonites and orthoceras is cut and polished. In the late afternoon you arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi near Merzouga. Leave your main luggage in the vehicle, mount your camel and ride for about an hour and a half into the dunes as the sand turns orange. Climb a dune for the sunset, then reach your camp for dinner, music around the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart the Dades valley.
10:00 – Todra gorge walk (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch in Tinghir or Tinejdad (not included).
14:30 – Erfoud; fossil workshop (optional).
16:30 – Camel trek into the dunes (about 1.5 hours).
18:30 – Sunset and dinner at the desert camp.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Pack a small bag for the night: toothbrush, warm layer, torch.
• Camps with a private bathroom in each tent are available on request.
• If you prefer not to ride, a 4x4 can take you to the camp.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the dunes, then north through the Ziz valley and over the Middle Atlas to the imperial city of Fes.

Wake before dawn and climb a dune to watch the sun rise over the Sahara, then ride the camels back to Merzouga, where you can shower at a partner hotel before breakfast. The road north passes Erfoud and Errachidia and enters the Ziz valley, a long green ribbon of palm groves and earthen ksour cut deep into the desert, with a superb viewpoint above the gorges. You cross the Tizi n'Talghemt pass and stop for lunch in Midelt, the apple town at the foot of the Jebel Ayachi. In the afternoon the road climbs into the Middle Atlas and the cedar forest near Azrou, home to troops of Barbary macaques, then passes Ifrane, a town of sloping roofs built in an alpine style at 1,650 m. You reach Fes in the late afternoon, where your driver drops you at your riad or hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise from the dunes; camel ride back (about 1 hour).
08:00 – Shower, breakfast and departure.
10:00 – Ziz valley viewpoint.
13:00 – Lunch in Midelt (not included).
15:00 – Cedar forest and the macaques.
15:45 – Ifrane.
17:30 – Drop-off at your riad or hotel in Fes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 470 km; your driver stops whenever you like.
• Please do not feed the macaques; it harms them.
• In winter the passes can see snow; your driver checks the road and may take the Boulemane route.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, drop-off in Fes.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips, accommodation in Fes.

Overnight: none (end of the tour in Fes).
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Where does the tour start and end?
faq.answer: It starts in Ouarzazate – at your hotel, the airport or the bus station – and ends at your riad or hotel in Fes in the late afternoon of Day 3.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle and driver are only for you and your group, and you can change the pace and stops each day.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Dinner and breakfast on both nights: at the hotel in the Dades valley and at the desert camp. Lunches are not included so you can choose where to stop.

faq.question: How long are the drives?
faq.answer: Day 1 is about 160 km with many stops, Day 2 about 300 km including the Todra gorge, and Day 3 about 470 km, a full day from Merzouga to Fes with stops in the Ziz valley, Midelt and the cedar forest.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: A camp of Berber-style tents in the Erg Chebbi dunes with real beds, blankets, dinner and breakfast. Camps with private bathrooms in each tent are available on request.

faq.question: Do I have to ride a camel?
faq.answer: No. The camel ride is about an hour and a half each way, but a 4x4 can take you to the camp if you prefer, or if someone has back problems.

faq.question: Can we visit Ait Ben Haddou?
faq.answer: Yes. If you have not seen it yet, we can add Ait Ben Haddou or the Atlas film studios on the morning of Day 1, with a slightly earlier start.

faq.question: Is a night in Fes included?
faq.answer: No, the tour ends with your drop-off in Fes. We can book a riad in the medina for you and arrange a guided day of Fes.

faq.question: Is this tour suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually love the camels, the dunes and the macaques. Day 3 is long, so bring entertainment for the car; child seats are available on request.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Layers for cold desert nights and possible snow in the Middle Atlas in winter, a small overnight bag for the camp, sunglasses, sunscreen, a scarf against wind and sand, and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). Winter is fine with warm clothes for the camp; in July and August the desert is very hot, so we start early.

faq.question: Can the tour be done in the other direction?
faq.answer: Yes, from Fes to Ouarzazate. Many travellers then continue to Ait Ben Haddou and Marrakech. Tell us your plans and we will adapt the route.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No, but they are few and modest on this route: a few dirhams for the Kasbah Amridil and optional fossil workshops, which are free to visit.
